A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLP research, with matching core methodology, experiments and proofs. The main text, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLP, CPT and RPT experiments, Qwen and Nemotron benchmark results, and corpus and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds larger-model and early-checkpoint results, additional controls, runtime measurements, perplexity evaluations and thought-trace analysis.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the shared policy/predictor, information-gain reward, corrected group advantages, clipped update and EMA rule. Sampling one target token per document and the generation prompt are newly documented implementation details, not established revisions to the algorithm.

E1.justification: Table S.8 adds language-modeling evaluation on Nemotron-CrossThink and the newly evaluated Wikitext-103 corpus. The original training corpora and downstream reasoning benchmarks remain; larger models and earlier checkpoints change configurations rather than dataset/task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 removes the untreated base-model comparator from the RPT comparison. Table 2 adds a post-trained Nemotron baseline, and Table S.7 introduces SFT as a direct runtime comparator. CPT and RPT remain the principal comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-14B, a Nemotron checkpoint pretrained on 4T tokens, Nemotron post-training, an 8K-versus-32K CPT control, and perplexity/NLL and runtime evaluations. Section 4 also distinguishes the retained OmniMath token-matched comparison from a new target/FLOP-matched CrossThink experiment, revising v1's blanket description of matched data and compute.

E4.justification: The original rollout, completion-length, KL and domain-mixture studies remain. New analyses examine early introduction of RLP, CPT context length, EMA decay, training efficiency, language-modeling preservation and 50 randomly sampled thought traces, substantially broadening diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report math Pass@1 averaged over eight runs and science greedy results plus Pass@1 over four runs. v2 introduces no new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 4, S.1 and S.2 retain their values, but v2 adds substantial results: Nemotron post-training overall scores of 65.31 versus 68.09, Qwen3-14B scores of 60.66 versus 65.00, and FLOP-matched RPT/RLP scores of 35.68 versus 42.86. Section 4 corrects Nemotron's relative gain from 35% to 43%. New Table S.9 reports OpenThoughts overall 40.66, conflicting with 41.45 in retained Table 4.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–3 and their proofs are retained. New Section 9 adds an unbiasedness derivation, replicator dynamics, a claimed monotonic expected-improvement argument for negative rewards, and a three-iteration numerical illustration.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: verifier-free information-gain pretraining, persistent benefits after post-training, cross-corpus generalization and architectural scalability. The additional experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions explain reinforcement of less harmful thoughts, argue that EMA and ground-truth likelihood prevent reward gaming, interpret longer-context CPT performance, and distinguish runtime overhead from FLOP efficiency. They also discuss early-pretraining applicability, data-lineage independence and thought quality, substantially extending v1's interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies one randomly selected rewarded token per document, provides the generation prompt, and expands compute accounting and timing details. These materially clarify implementation despite retaining the main hyperparameter recipe. The RLP code link in v1's abstract is removed; this does not establish that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds Han et al.'s reward-based-pretraining position paper and supporting model/data-lineage references such as Phi-4, Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3 and Nemotron-4. The main Related Work section and positioning against RPT remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing main-text prose and section order remain intact. Revisions concentrate on scaling and RPT passages, terminology and header updates, appendix renumbering, and added explanatory subsections rather than a broad rewrite of the original narrative.

P2.justification: The NVIDIA report layout is replaced by the ICLR conference format. Table 2 expands into a full benchmark/post-training matrix, Table 3 separates matching regimes, and Tables S.3–S.9 plus prompt and trace boxes are added. Figures 1–2 retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful scaling experiments, controls and crucial sampling/prompt disclosures. However, its new Section 9 monotonicity argument does not establish the claimed guarantee for the shared predictor's parameter-dependent rewards. New reporting conflicts also weaken reliability: Table S.9 contradicts Table 4 for OpenThoughts, and Section 12 attributes 35.60 to the 6B CPT baseline whose Table 4 score is 38.04. These substantive benefits and new reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
